implemented: One-sided normal-approximation sample size uses detectable daily benefit, daily volatility, target power and familywise alpha divided across pre-registered looks.
Dependence design effect and expected usable-session rate increase the required session count.
The required sample is max(session floor, calculated adjusted requirement); the default 60 sessions is not treated as sufficient by itself.
The plan reports estimated power at the floor, the assumption values, a freeze-before-observation check and a stable SHA-256 identity.
limitations: The detectable benefit, volatility, dependence design effect and expected observation rate are caller-supplied, not empirically fitted here.
The formula uses a normal approximation; it does not replace cohort-level dependence-robust inference or the final promotion gate.
No prospective trading performance or profitability is implied.
